analysis.file_name: BofA - Global Nuclear - Urenco USA site visit - a growing global leader in uranium enrichment services - 2026-10-29.pdf
analysis.title: Global Nuclear: Urenco USA site visit: a growing global leader in uranium enrichment services
key_insights: BofA hosted an investor site visit to Urenco USA in New Mexico. It sees Urenco's growing enrichment order book as a positive signal for Buy-rated Cameco (CCJ) and Neutral-rated Centrus (LEU). Urenco's expansion experience points to substantial capex for smaller developers, and its contracting experience supports more US enrichment supply.
Urenco's enrichment order book rose to €27.3bn at 30-Jun-26 from €21.3bn at year-end 2025, €18.7bn at year-end 2024 and €14.7bn at year-end 2023. The contract book now extends to 2050.

Conversion and natural uranium suppliers such as CCJ have seen more subdued contract book growth. BofA thinks US utilities, because of the Russian import ban, are securing enrichment first and will turn to conversion and natural uranium later. As enricher books fill, BofA expects converter and miner books to grow faster.

Urenco announced on 2-Jun-26 a 2.1m SWU capacity expansion at its New Mexico site, nearly 50% of the site's capacity. Construction starts in 2029 and completes in 2036. It adds to a 700k SWU expansion announced 6-Jul-23 that completes next year. The order book is described as very full through 2034.
The 2.1m SWU expansion should cost about $2bn, or roughly $1bn per m SWU. Replacement value of the entire New Mexico facility as a first-of-a-kind build is $10-$11bn, or $2-$2.2bn per m SWU.

Demand for LEU from the existing fleet is healthy. Longer refueling cycles and power uprates create incremental LEU+ demand. Constellation, Southern, NextEra, PSEG and Vistra are cited as pursuing 24-month cycles or uprates.

Urenco has signed LEU+ and HALEU contracts with new nuclear customers: Ontario Power Generation (up to four BWRX-300 SMRs), Jimmy Energy, Standard Nuclear (first deliveries targeted 2027), Radiant and Antares Nuclear (first long-term multi-year commercial HALEU contract, May 2026).

Enrichment supply growth by 2030 vs 2025: CNNC +85%, Orano +19%, Urenco +7%. Demand is expected to outstrip supply in 2030 until Orano adds supply in 2031. Supply to the US market is expected to fall short of US demand. General Matter and Global Laser Enrichment supply is not expected until 2037.
BofA thinks global enrichment markets are tightening rapidly, which should raise U3O8 demand through more overfeeding, and that a new all-time high for U3O8 is feasible.

Conversion pricing is down from the February 2024 highs of $97 (NA) and $95 (EU) to about $60/KgU. BofA sees possible near- to medium-term appreciation given tight supply: Kazatomprom's 10% curtailment, the Russian import ban, and Orano's Philippe Coste output falling to 9kt from 13kt in 2025.

Brokers, traders and other financial institutions made up about 74% of 2025 spot purchase volumes, up from 60% in 2005. Producers' share of term selling volumes fell from 92% in 2023 to 76% in 2025, which BofA reads as rising utility participation supporting prices.
Urenco's 2025 revenue was split 50% US, 35% rest of Europe, 10% rest of world and 5% UK. Enrichment revenue was €2,096m in 2025.
Urenco is owned in thirds by the UK government, the Dutch government and Uranit UK (E.ON and RWE equally). Treaty structure restricts control and transfer of its enrichment technology.

market_movers.rationale: Urenco's growing enrichment order book is a positive read-through, and BofA expects conversion and miner contract books to grow faster as enricher books fill. PO is based on 1.0x NAV and 35.0x 2026E and 34.5x 2027E EV/EBITDA.
Urenco's order book is a positive signal for Centrus, and its expansion cost points to substantial capex for smaller enrichers. PO is 2.5x estimated 2026E NAV.
PO is based on a sum-of-the-parts. Cited for Calvert Cliffs 24-month cycles and uprate agreements with Google (890 MW across 11 reactors) and Amazon (190 MW at Calvert Cliffs).
PO is based on a sum-of-the-parts. Cited for pursuing a 24-month cycle at St. Lucie Unit 2.
PO is based on a 2028 sum-of-the-parts. Cited for a 24-month-cycle transition at Hope Creek.
PO is based on a 2028 sum-of-the-parts. Cited for a Vogtle Units 1 & 2 NRC pathway contemplating enrichment above 5% U-235 and potential 24-month cycles.
PO is based on a DCF with contracted, qualified and future-market cash flow buckets. Urenco has an LEU+ contract with Standard Nuclear, with first deliveries targeted for 2027.
PO is based on a 2028E EBITDA sum-of-the-parts. Plans 433 MW of nuclear uprates at Beaver Valley, Davis-Besse and Perry, with about 200 MW of potential further uprates at Comanche Peak.

sector_views.rationale: Enrichment is tightening, the order book is growing, and conversion and U3O8 are expected to follow. The US market is short of enrichment supply because of the Russian import ban.

earnings_insights: Urenco is private. Its enrichment order book was €27.3bn at 30-Jun-26, versus €21.3bn at year-end 2025 (reported).
Urenco 2025 revenue by geography (reported): US €1,057m, UK €97m, rest of Europe €740m, rest of world €202m. Enrichment business revenue was €2,096m in 2025.
BofA's Centrus PO of $167 uses 2.5x 2026E NAV (estimate). It cites the early-2026 $900m DoE funding award.
BofA's Cameco PO of C$190 uses 35.0x 2026E and 34.5x 2027E EV/EBITDA (estimates) plus 1.0x NAV.

macro_indicators.interpretation: BofA's annual average forecast, up 34% y/y.
BofA forecasts a further 33% y/y rise, the peak of its forecast path.
Prices ease 14% y/y but stay strong.
Spot trades below the $96.00/lb long-term price as of September 2026, which BofA reads as healthy but not excessive utility demand.
Down from the $97 all-time high but still elevated.

risk_factors: Cameco downside: slower global energy demand growth, continued delay in Japanese reactor restarts, worse nuclear sentiment or a shift to other fuels, and production problems at Cigar Lake.
Centrus downside: lower enrichment pricing, loss of access to enriched uranium product, restrictive regulation or sanctions, shipping disruptions and technical disruptions.
Smaller enrichers face substantial capex, with Urenco's expansion at roughly $1bn per m SWU and a first-of-a-kind build at $2-$2.2bn per m SWU.
BofA notes that in the 2004-07 cycle a correction followed once supply and demand balanced. It sees this occurring only when the uranium deficit levels out, with risk of that being extended.
Orano's Philippe Coste plant has had a slower ramp and a three-month outage, cutting 2026 output to 9kt from 13kt.
charts_described: Exhibit 6 plots enrichment facility supply and demand 2025-2045 in million SWU, and shows US supply short of US demand given the Russian import ban.
Exhibit 14 shows BofA's U3O8 forecasts: $97.40/lb in 2026E and $129.80/lb in 2027E, easing to $84.75/lb by 2031E.
Exhibit 15 shows spot U3O8 at $90.00/lb below the long-term price of $96.00/lb as of September 2026.
vol_and_positioning: The Sprott Physical Uranium Trust (SPUT) historically led U3O8 spot increases through purchases, but that relationship has weakened. SPUT purchases slow when it trades at a discount to NAV.
Brokers, traders and other financial institutions were about 74% of 2025 spot purchase volumes. Spot volumes have fallen 40% since 2020 while term volumes rose 102%.
geopolitical: The US ban on imports of Russian uranium products leaves US enrichment supply short of US demand.

Urenco's ownership and technology transfers are overseen by a UK, German and Dutch government Joint Committee under the Treaty of Almelo, with similar safeguards in the Treaties of Washington and Cardiff.
CNNC is adding a sixth centrifuge enrichment plant at Lanzhou, driving 85% enrichment supply growth by 2030 vs 2025.
Kazatomprom's 10% production curtailment keeps conversion and uranium supply tight.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA sees enrichment tightening rapidly, conversion tight with Kazatomprom curtailing 10% and Orano output down, and a feasible new all-time high for U3O8. Its forecasts reach $129.80/lb in 2027E.
tension_points.bear_case: Spot has moderated in the mid $80s over the past month, and the 2004-07 cycle saw a correction once supply and demand balanced. Spot is below the long-term price of $96.00/lb. SPUT purchases have slowed at NAV discounts and its link to spot has weakened.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A correction once the uranium deficit levels out, which BofA says would occur only then, with risk of that being extended.
